ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $3.74 Ryde voucher to the rider (per NS-7, voucher form) for the two unexempted detour segments; note the driver's RD-1 shortest-route breach on file (no account flag — RD-6 threshold not met).

segment_findings.reason: Off-route 22:57–23:03, +1.14 km. No RD-5 consent: the only pre-departure chats (22:40) are pickup logistics [F8][F9]; no route change was proposed or agreed. No RD-4 reasonable cause: speed band 3 on East Coast Parkway [F11] is not band 1/2 and no route incident was recorded [F13]. Unexempted per RD-1/RD-2.

Off-route 23:21–23:24, +1.51 km (up to 985 m off route). Same analysis: no rider agreement (RD-5), and the Airport Boulevard band 3 record [F12] does not meet RD-4(b) and there is no traffic-incident support [F13]. Driver's 'GPS rerouted me' [F10] is not a reasonable cause. Unexempted per RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's statement that following GPS rerouting justifies the fare — rejected: RD-4 requires traffic evidence tied to the replaced optimal-route segment; only band 3 speeds [F11][F12] and no incidents [F13] exist, and mere GPS rerouting is not a 'reasonable cause' under RD-1.

Billed excess of $4.41 covers the full +3.1 km; the 0.20 km gap between the two segments' 2.65 km and the billed 3.1 km is map-matching residual and is not refundable under RD-2, so only $3.74 is refunded.
Driver profile cited for RD-6 account flag — not applicable: route disputes upheld in 90 d = 0, so the 'repeated route deviation' precondition fails, and profile facts cannot alone decide the case.
Extra duration of 21.8 min — no separate refund: time-based waiting is charged at $0.00 [F7] and RD-2 refunds only the mileage units of the unexempted segments.
